item.aggregatedOutput:
# Build cache notes

The CI job restores its dependency cache from a key made of the runner image and the branch name.
When the lockfile changes the key stays the same, so the restored store no longer matches it and
the install step refuses it. Rebuilding by hand fixes one run, then the next lockfile change breaks it again.

## Ideas

- hash the lockfile into the key;
- keep a restore key without the hash, so most packages still come from the cache;
- share one store between branches that have the same lockfile.

item.text:
The CI cache key uses the runner image and branch name. When the lockfile changes, CI restores a dependency store built for the old lockfile, and the install step rejects it. Rebuilding the cache by hand fixes only that run.

Adding the lockfile hash to the cache key gives each lockfile version its own cache entry. A fallback key can still let CI reuse packages from an older cache, provided the install step validates them against the current lockfile. I appended the exact review line to `notes.md`.

- Confirm that a lockfile change produces a different cache key.
- Confirm that an unchanged lockfile gives an exact cache hit.
- Confirm that a fallback restore still lets the install complete against the current lockfile.
